programme.desc: Live. Patrick Vieira revisits the defining moments of his legendary Premier League career, counting down the 10 greatest memories from his time in England. From fierce rivalries and title triumphs to unforgettable performances in midfield, Vieira reflects on the moments that shaped his legacy as one of the Premier League's all-time greats.

programme.title: NETBUSTERS - MW11 - EP11
programme.desc: Live. A fast-paced music and commentary driven ISO angle highlights show featuring every game and every goal from each match round.

programme.title: THE CATCH-UP SHOW - EP14
programme.desc: Live. The Catch-Up Show is your chance to relive the 'best bits' from across the Premier League week with a compilation of all PLP content and programming.

programme.title: PL REWIND - EP8
programme.desc: Live. Darren Bent is one of a select number of players to have scored a century of goals in the Premier League. The prolific striker recalls his days at Ipswich, Charlton, Spurs, Sunderland, and Aston Villa and the goals he scored on his way to joining that elite group.

programme.title: CLASSIC MATCH - SUN v TOT
programme.desc: Live. We delve into the Premier League archive to bring you a Classic Match from the 2009/2010 season.

programme.title: Tottenham Hotspur vs Ipswich Town (MW11) - Premier League 2026/27
programme.desc: Live. Spurs have lost four of their last five Premier League games against Ipswich, though the exception was a 4-1 win in their last meeting in February 2025.

programme.title: Hull City vs Brighton and Hove Albion (MW11) - Premier League 2026/27
programme.desc: Live. Brighton are winless in all six of their visits to the MKM Stadium in all competitions (D2 L4). Their last away win against Hull came at Boothferry Park in the fourth tier in October 2000.

programme.title: PL Rewind 2026/27 - EP7
programme.desc: Live. David James is one of the Premier League’s most memorable goalkeepers. Few can match the England international for his longevity in the top flight, where he played with distinction between 1992 and 2010. He shares his memories of the key matches and best saves of his career.

programme.title: PL Stories 2026/27 - EP25
programme.desc: Live. We follow Nemanja Matic’s journey from his upbringing in Serbia to Premier League success with Chelsea and his time at Manchester United. He reflects on the experiences that shaped him, the challenges of establishing himself at the highest level and the managers who influenced his career. Through his story, we explore what it took to become a key figure in midfield for club and country.

programme.title: Liverpool vs Manchester United (MW11) - Premier League 2026/27 (4K)
programme.desc: Live. Liverpool lost both Premier League meetings with Manchester United last season, as many as they had in their previous 18 (W7 D9). They last lost more consecutively between December 2014 and January 2016 (4).

programme.title: Chelsea vs Leeds United (MW11) - Premier League 2026/27
programme.desc: Live. Chelsea have won eight of their last 10 home games against Leeds in all competitions (D2) since a 2-0 loss in December 1999. They’ve already beaten the Whites 6-3 at Stamford Bridge in the EFL Cup this season.

programme.title: Live NFL
programme.desc: Detroit Lions v Chicago Bears (Kick-off 6.00pm). Coverage of the week 12 match from Ford Field. The Lions have played a home game on Thanksgiving Day almost every year since 1934, with the only exceptions being six years during World War II. The tradition began when then-owner George A. Richards wanted to build excitement and draw attention ahead of a match against the unbeaten Chicago Bears, and it proved to be so successful it was broadcast by 94 radio stations across the country, becoming the first-ever national NFL radio broadcast.

programme.title: Live NFL
programme.desc: Dallas Cowboys v Philadelphia Eagles (Kick-off 9.30pm). Coverage of the week 12 match from AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas. The Cowboys first played a Thanksgiving Day fixture in 1966 and have done so every year since then, except for 1975 and 1977. They come into this year's match having won in each of the last three years, including a 31-28 victory over the Kansas City Chiefs 12 months ago.

Recurring segments include the FCC-pleasing This Week in Unnecessary Censorship in which they take TV clips and "bleep and blur things whether they need it or not," as Kimmel describes it. programme.title: Yellowjackets
programme.desc: "Yellowjackets" tells the narrative of a team of wildly talented high-school girls soccer players who survive a plane crash deep in the Ontario wilderness. The series chronicles their descent from a complicated but thriving team to warring, cannibalistic clans, while also tracking the lives they have attempted to piece back together. Sophie Nélisse, Jasmin Savoy Brown, Sophie Thatcher and Sammi Hanratty star as the teenagers, while Melanie Lynskey, Tawny Cypress, Christina Ricci and Juliette Lewis portray their adult counterparts as they reveal the truth about their survival 25 years later.

programme.title: Live: Hot Stove
programme.desc: Baby, it might be cold outside, and the springtime sounds of bats hitting balls are months away. What better way for baseball fans to cure the winter blues than to gather around the "Hot Stove" and warm up to the news of the offseason? MLB Network has all the angles covered for all 30 teams, from trades and free agent signings to the juicy rumors that percolate throughout, especially at the annual Winter Meetings in December. A host of former players, including Joe Magrane, Al Leiter, Sean Casey and Dan Plesac, analyze the news, supplemented by insider information from journalists Jon Heyman, Tom Verducci and Peter Gammons, among others.

programme.title: 7 Little Johnstons
programme.desc: The Johnstons -- all seven -- of Forsyth, Ga., are the subjects of this reality-documentary series. The brood, TLC says, are "the world's largest known family of achondroplasia dwarfs." Achondroplasia is a genetic disorder of bone growth, but the series demonstrates that size only matters in the amount of love the Johnstons provide. Trent, a grounds supervisor at a local college, and housewife Amber have two biological children -- Jonah and Elizabeth -- while Anna, Alex and Emma were adopted from Russia, Korea and China, respectively. Episodes deal with everything from high-drama soccer tryouts to a disastrous attempt at a "birds and bees" discussion, all framed by the family tackling a massive renovation of their 6,000-square-foot, circa 1891 home.

La serie se transmite en tres ediciones nocturnas, luego se re-transmite la última edición cuatro veces cada mañana de lunes a viernes antes de despejar el escenario para un bloque de seis horas de "SportsCenter" en vivo, que pone más énfasis en la interactividad de los fanáticos, noticias, análisis, comentarios y la cobertura de las conferencias de prensa.
